newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares embark on another record day.
newsitem.headline: German shares embark on another record day.

text.p: German shares shot higher yet again in early trade on Wednesday, powering to fresh records amid a whole range of positive market factors, and dealers said they saw no signs that the market would break its uptrend.
"There seems to be nothing around to brake us at the moment," said a Frankfurt trader.
"The dollar is giving us a push, Bunds are helping, the U.S. is helping and there are no negative corporate stories out there. I don't see any justification for pulling out, even at these highs."
The 30-share DAX index was up 45.21 points, or 1.1 percent, at a record 4,051.61 points, having slipped marginally from a high of 4,064.93 points set in the pre-bourse session.
Several research houses were targeting 4,100 points on the DAX today but many traders were sceptical.
Some had already been caught wrongfooted by the continued rise in the DAX over the 4,000 point level, which many had seen as a natural peak.
"I could see maybe 10 or 20 more points in it. We have done quite a lot already," one trader said.
Shares were higher across the board.
Retailer Metro, already in favour after saying it might buy a Dutch cash and carry firm, posted further gains, rising some three percent to 225 marks.
The company, whose shareholder meeting takes place today, said it expected its operating profit this year to exceed the 1.06 billion marks it achieved in 1996.
Dealers said analysts at several German research houses had recommended the stock.
